ROLE: Append a complete SUBACK packet echoing the SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier and carrying one result code per filter in the order the filters appeared.

SIGNATURE.RAW: int wire_encode_suback(struct byte_buf *out, uint16_t packet_id, const uint8_t *codes, size_t count)
SIGNATURE.NAME: wire_encode_suback

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: destination for the encoded packet bytes

FUNC.NAME: buffer_reserve
FUNC.ROLE: allocate the whole packet before the first byte is written

FUNC.NAME: buffer_append
FUNC.ROLE: append the fixed header, the Packet Identifier bytes and the result codes

FUNC.NAME: wire_write_remaining_length
FUNC.ROLE: append the Remaining Length encoding of 2 + count

VAR.NAME: WIRE_MAX_STRING_LENGTH
VAR.ROLE: 65535; the largest accepted number of result codes

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_write_remaining_length
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: static int wire_write_remaining_length(struct byte_buf *out, size_t value)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 after appending the minimal 1..4 byte 7-bit-per-byte encoding of value; -1 when value exceeds 268435455 or the buffer cannot grow
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no ownership transfer; the bytes are appended to the caller's buffer
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: nonzero means no complete packet is written, so the caller returns -2 after having reserved the full packet size

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_reserve
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when cap >= len + extra; -1 on overflow or allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 leaves the contents unchanged, so the caller returns -2 without writing any byte

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_append
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int buffer_append(struct byte_buf *buf, const void *src, size_t len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when all len bytes were appended; -1 when nothing was appended
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no transfer; the code bytes are copied
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: cannot fail after the full-packet reserve; a -1 is propagated as -2

LOGIC.INPUT: out: caller-owned buffer. packet_id: the nonzero Packet Identifier of the SUBSCRIBE being answered. codes: count result bytes in filter order. count: number of filters, at least 1.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out is NULL or codes is NULL return -1. 2) If count == 0 return -1 (MQTT-3.9.3-1 requires at least one return code, matching the at-least-one-pair SUBSCRIBE rule); if count > 65535 return -1; if packet_id == 0 return -1 (the echoed identifier must be nonzero, MQTT-2.3.1-1). 3) For every i < count: if codes[i] is not one of 0x00, 0x01, 0x02 or 0x80 return -1 (only these four SUBACK return codes exist). All argument validation happens before the first byte is written. 4) body = 2 + count; rl_width = (body < 128) ? 1 : (body < 16384) ? 2 : (body < 2097152) ? 3 : 4; if buffer_reserve(out, 1 + rl_width + body) != 0 return -2. 5) hdr = (WIRE_PACKET_SUBACK << 4) = 0x90; buffer_append(out, &hdr, 1); wire_write_remaining_length(out, body); pid_hi = (uint8_t)(packet_id >> 8); pid_lo = (uint8_t)(packet_id & 0xFF); buffer_append(out, &pid_hi, 1); buffer_append(out, &pid_lo, 1); buffer_append(out, codes, count). Any nonzero return after the reserve means the packet is incomplete: return -2 and let the caller discard the buffer. 6) Return 0. The codes array order is the filter order, so result i corresponds to the i-th filter/QoS pair of the SUBSCRIBE payload.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when 0x90, the Remaining Length of 2 + count, the two identifier bytes (MSB first) and count result codes were appended in that order. -1 for a NULL out/codes, count 0, count above 65535, a zero packet_id or an undefined result code, with nothing written. -2 when the buffer could not be grown even though the arguments were valid. This broker always passes count = number of filters and codes[i] = 0x00, producing 90 03 00 01 00 for the single-filter SUBSCRIBE with Packet Identifier 1.
INVARIANTS_USED: SUBACK has fixed header flags 0 and Remaining Length 2 + number of filters
the SUBACK Packet Identifier equals the nonzero SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier (MQTT-3.9.2-1)
one result code per filter, in the order the filters appeared (MQTT-3.9.3-1)
a queue append preserves already queued bytes
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: out is NULL or a valid byte_buf; codes points to count readable result bytes when count > 0.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: on success the SUBACK is appended after the bytes already queued; on -1 nothing changed; on -2 no complete packet was appended.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns out exclusively.

WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: 0x90: type 9 in the high nibble, reserved flag bits 0 in the low nibble.
minimal 7-bit-per-byte encoding of 2 + count (1 byte below 128, 2 bytes below 16384, ...), produced by wire_write_remaining_length.

WIRE_MAPPING.TARGET: the two bytes after the Remaining Length
WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: packet_id written MSB first; it must equal the identifier of the answered SUBSCRIBE and must not be zero.

WIRE_MAPPING.WIRE_FIELD: Payload: one return code per filter
WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: one byte per filter in filter order; each byte must be 0x00, 0x01, 0x02 or 0x80. This broker grants QoS 0 for every filter, so every byte is 0x00 (scope R03/R04).

EXPECT.derivation: 0x90 | Remaining Length 2 + 1 = 3 -> 0x03 | identifier 0x0001 MSB first | one result code 0x00
Remaining Length 2 + 2 = 4 | identifier 42 = 0x002A | codes in filter order, both granted QoS 0
Remaining Length 2 + 126 = 128 -> seven-bit groups 128 % 128 = 0 with continuation then 128 / 128 = 1, i.e. 0x80 0x01

cases.note: a SUBACK needs at least one code
0x03 is not a SUBACK return code
0x81 is not a SUBACK return code
